content: Anabaena is a genus of filamentous cyanobacteria, also known as blue-green algae, that exists as plankton in aquatic environments. This genus is particularly notable for its ability to fix atmospheric nitrogen, a process that allows it to convert nitrogen gas into forms usable by living organisms. Anabaena forms symbiotic relationships with certain plants, such as the mosquito fern (Azolla), where it contributes to nitrogen enrichment. Anabaena is one of four genera of cyanobacteria capable of producing neurotoxins. These neurotoxins can be harmful to local wildlife, as well as to farm animals and pets, posing ecological and agricultural risks. The genome of Anabaena is approximately 2 million base pairs in length. A key feature of Anabaena is the presence of specialized cells called heterocysts. These cells are terminally differentiated and are responsible for nitrogen fixation. Under nitrogen-limiting conditions, vegetative cells along the filament differentiate into heterocysts at semi-regular intervals. The interior of heterocysts is microoxic, a condition achieved through increased respiration, the inactivation of oxygen-producing photosystem II, and the development of a thickened envelope outside the cell wall. These adaptations create an environment conducive to the activity of nitrogenase, the enzyme responsible for converting atmospheric dinitrogen (N₂) into ammonium (NH₄⁺). This process requires energy in the form of ATP and reducing power, both of which are derived from carbohydrate metabolism. In the presence of light, photosystem I further supplements this process. Carbohydrates, likely in the form of sucrose, are synthesized in the vegetative cells and transported into the heterocysts to fuel nitrogen fixation. In return, the fixed nitrogen, at least partially in the form of amino acids, is transported back from the heterocysts to the vegetative cells, ensuring a mutual exchange of resources within the filament. Certain species of Anabaena have been utilized in rice paddy fields as a natural fertilizer, demonstrating their effectiveness in enhancing soil fertility through nitrogen fixation. The genus Anabaena includes numerous species, such as Anabaena azollae, Anabaena flos-aquae, Anabaena circinalis, and Anabaena variabilis, among others. Each species exhibits unique characteristics and ecological roles, contributing to the diversity and functionality of this genus in various environments.
